data.name: Remiel
data.gender_notes: Remiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Remiel means 'God's comfort'. In the Old Testament, Raphael, another angel, is identified as 'God's healer'. Remiel, meaning 'God''s comfort', may have been an alternative name for Raphael. The name Remiel carries the meaning “God's comfort” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Remiel usually hope their child will grow to embody god's comfort and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that evokes a sense of God's presence and comfort.
data.etymology: Remiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's comfort.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Remiel total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Remiel was an angelic name used in early Jewish and Christian doctrine, representing divine comfort and healing. In medieval Europe, Remiel was believed to be the angel of mercy. Remiel's sympathetic presence is evident in literature, art, and even heraldry, signifying kindness, compassion, healing, and solace.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Remiel stands as a reminder of God's comforting presence during difficult times. The name's spiritual significance has a deep and personal meaning, as it suggests that God is not only compassionate but also actively involved in our lives, providing us with consolation and solace when we are in need. The name Remiel thus holds immense spiritual significance, as it encourages believers to look to God for comfort and healing.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Remiel means "God's compassion" in Hebrew, symbolizing the angel's role as a comforting presence and a bearer of God's mercy and love.

biblical_reference.note: not directly mentioned in the Bible, but appears in apocryphal texts

historical_references.reference: In the apocryphal book of 'The Book of Enoch', Remiel is mentioned as one of the seven holy angels who intercede for human beings before the throne of God.
historical_references.context: The Book of Enoch is an ancient Jewish text believed to have been written around 200 BC. It is not considered part of the biblical canon by most Christian denominations, but it has had significant influence on Christian and Jewish thought.

historical_references.reference: Remiel is also mentioned in the 'Golden Legend' as a patron saint of the dead and the guardian of the seventh heaven. According to this legend, Remiel intercedes for the souls of the deceased before God.
historical_references.context: The 'Golden Legend' is a collection of hagiographical texts compiled by Jacobus de Voragine in the 13th century. It includes stories about saints and other holy figures, and has been used as a source of devotional material in the Catholic Church.

Angel enthusiasts and spiritual seekers frequently delve into the symbolism and significance of Remiel's name and role.
